competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight, the desk reads a firm but not panic-risk tape: Brent 104.77 and WTI 96.46 keep an energy premium in place while gold at 3969.60 and equities near recent highs (Nasdaq 25164, Dow 51983) argue investors are not de-risking hard; VIX 19.42 sits in a moderate band. Cash SOFR is 3.95 percent and the 2027 strip still embeds additional tightening (June 4.47, December 4.475), consistent with a Federal Reserve that held in late October and sounded firm on inflation even as the 10-year drifted higher. Gulf logistics remain the swing factor: Iran mining claims and earlier strike headlines versus safe-passage diplomacy and a thin supply-buffer warning. The Bank of Japan held with underlying inflation at 2 percent for the first time since 2013; New Zealand's late-October surprise still echoes in a kiwi that is very cheap on five-year ranges. AI-linked credit headlines add a financing angle without a clear risk-off trigger. Consumer and activity coverage for Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the euro area, and Japan is incomplete — a research caveat, not a reason to stand down from markable markets.

lesson_considerations.rationale: That rule is about an AUDCAD richness fade that needed housing or Bank of Canada path time longer than an overnight clock, and about not flipping the same Australia-Canada cross. This ticket is a from-flat AUDNZD short at a 99.6 five-year extreme. It is Australia versus New Zealand, not Australia versus Canada, and it is opened as a multi-week swing rather than a two-to-three-day fade of the just-closed Canada cross.

That rule says stay flat after closing AUDCAD until a new Australia-versus-Canada policy, growth, inflation, or carry gap appears. This open is not a reverse of that Canada cross and does not use oil or diplomacy as a reason to own CAD. It fades Australia-New Zealand richness on a markable cross after the late-October New Zealand surprise already cheapened kiwi.

lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The edge is the extreme cross location versus a 3.5-percentile NZDUSD that mixes in the dollar; it is exhausted if AUDNZD holds a new high through 1.2456 or if a New Zealand cash or policy gap starts paying Australia as hard as the listed Australia-Canada cash wedge.
lifecycle.realization_logic: AUDNZD pays if the 99.6 five-year richness fades over weeks as New Zealand cheapness is expressed against Australia rather than against the dollar, not as a two-to-three-day mean-reversion spike.

spot_candidate.rationale: Short AUDNZD at 1.2456, a 99.6 five-year percentile, isolates Australia-versus-New Zealand richness better than fading NZDUSD at 0.5627 or fading AUDCAD 0.9793 against a 205 basis-point cash gap.

cross-merchant.thesis: Australian dollar versus New Zealand dollar at 1.2456 is a 99.6 five-year percentile while the kiwi versus the dollar at 0.5627 is a 3.5 five-year percentile, so the dollar pair mixes New Zealand cheapness with a United States leg and the cross is the cleaner Australia-versus-New Zealand expression. Australian dollar-Canada at 0.9793 is only a 90th percentile, cash Australia 4.60 versus Canada 2.55 still pays 205 basis points to Australia, and Brent 104.77 supports Canada on oil without a new Australia-Canada policy gap. Short the Australia-New Zealand cross from a flat book.
